channel.title: Mercedes-Benz recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Door Lock Defect May Cause Rollaway
item.description: Certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles have a micro-switch in the driver's door lock that can corrode. When this happens, the switch may fail to detect that the door is open, which can prevent the electronic parking brake's Auto-Park feature from engaging on its own. Without the parking brake engaging automatically, the vehicle may roll away on its own.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Instrument Panel Display May Go Blank
item.description: The system that controls the infotainment screen may reset on its own while the vehicle is being driven. When this happens, the instrument panel display can go blank, meaning the driver can no longer see it.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz E-Class and S-Class Drive Shaft Joint Failure
item.description: On certain Mercedes-Benz E 400 4MATIC, E 450 4MATIC, E 450 4MATIC Coupe, and S 560 4MATIC vehicles, a universal joint in the drive shaft may break. If this joint breaks, the vehicle can suddenly lose the power that turns the wheels while it is being driven, meaning the car stops being able to move under its own power at that moment.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz G580 EV Wheel Bolts May Fail
item.description: During manufacturing, the wrong bolts may have been used to attach the wheels on these vehicles. Bolts that are not the correct type may not hold the wheel as securely as they should. If this happens, a wheel could become loose or detach from the vehicle while you are driving.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz GLA 250 door may not open inside
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain GLA 250 vehicles. A cable that works the door latch may have been installed incorrectly. When that happens, the door cannot be opened from inside the vehicle. Dealers will inspect the cable assembly and repair it if needed, at no charge to the owner. Owner letters were mailed May 1, 2026, and the vehicle identification numbers covered by this recall can be searched on NHTSA.gov beginning March 13, 2026.

item.title: Mercedes EQB High Voltage Battery Can Catch Fire
item.description: Certain Mercedes-Benz EQB vehicles have a high voltage battery that may fail internally. This kind of internal battery failure can lead to a vehicle fire, and this can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven at the time.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz EQB Electric Battery Fire Risk
item.description: The high-voltage battery in some EQB 300 4MATIC and EQB 350 4MATIC vehicles can fail on the inside. This internal failure can lead to a fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven. Some vehicles that were already repaired under an earlier recall will need to be repaired again. Mercedes-Benz dealers will update the software that manages the battery, free of charge.

item.title: Mercedes GLE 350 Rear Seat Belt Won't Lock Child Seat
item.description: On some 2025-2026 GLE 350 4MATIC vehicles, the center rear seat belts may have been installed without a feature required to lock a child restraint properly in place. This means that if a child seat or booster is installed in the center rear seat, the seat belt may not hold it securely. Dealers will replace the center rear seat belt assembly to fix this, free of charge.

item.title: Mercedes G63 Radar Sensor May Disable Safety Features
item.description: Some AMG G63 and G580 SUVs have a front radar sensor with a circuit board that can fail. This sensor helps power several driver assistance features, including automatic emergency braking, active brake assist, lane keeping assist, and Distronic cruise control. If the sensor fails, these features may stop working. Without automatic emergency braking working as intended, the vehicle may not brake automatically to help avoid a crash, increasing the risk of a collision.

item.title: Mercedes EQE and GLC steering coupling bolt may loosen
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain EQE and GLC models because the bolt that holds the steering coupling together may not have been properly tightened. This can allow the steering coupling to loosen and come apart from the steering rack.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz EQB Loss Of Drive Power Risk
item.description: Some Mercedes-Benz EQB 300 4MATIC and EQB 350 4MATIC electric SUVs have a bus bar in the high-voltage battery that may be secured with the wrong screws. This can cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power while you're driving, without any warning beforehand.

item.title: Mercedes GLC Roof Pillar May Not Absorb Crash Impact
item.description: Some Mercedes-Benz GLC models built with a panoramic sunroof have a problem with a roof pillar next to the back seat, called the C-pillar. In certain types of crashes, a rear passenger's head can strike that pillar, and the pillar may not soak up enough of the impact. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for protection inside the vehicle. Dealers will change the roof lining and the C-pillar trim free of charge.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz models make wrong pedestrian warning sound in reverse
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain electric and plug-in models, including the EQS SUV and S-Class. These vehicles have a system that makes an artificial sound outside the car so that people nearby can hear it coming. A software problem can make the car play the wrong sound while it is backing up, which means the vehicles do not meet the federal rule on minimum sound for hybrid and electric vehicles. Dealers will update the software free of charge.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz GLE, GLS Rearview Mirror May Detach
item.description: Certain Mercedes-Benz GLE and GLS SUVs have a multi-purpose camera and a rearview mirror that are mounted on the windshield. These parts may not be attached firmly enough, and either one could come loose over time. If the mirror detaches, the driver is left with less visibility. If the camera detaches, features such as Active Lane Keeping Assist and Active Brake Assist may stop working.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz C 300 seat belt anchor may loosen
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain C 300 and AMG C 43 vehicles because the driver-side seat belt cover may not be properly installed on the seat belt tensioner. If the cover is not installed correctly, it can cause the seat belt anchor to come loose. A loose anchor means the seat belt may not stay fully secured in place the way it is supposed to.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz G-Class Stability Warning Light May Be Wrong
item.description: If the electronic stability program has a failure, the warning light on the dashboard may not display correctly. This means the light may not properly show that there is a problem with the stability control system.

item.title: Mercedes Sprinter Parking Brake Bracket Welds May Fail
item.description: Daimler Vans is recalling certain 2024 Sprinter vans. The welds on the parking brake cable bracket may fail, which can cause the parking brake to disengage on its own.

item.title: Mercedes EQB Battery Failure Can Cause Fire
item.description: Certain Mercedes-Benz EQB electric vehicles have a high voltage battery that may fail internally. This kind of internal failure can lead to a vehicle fire, and this can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz E 350 Rear Axle Weld Defect
item.description: A metal bracket that connects to the rear axle on some E 350 and E 350 4MATIC vehicles may not have been welded onto the axle correctly. Because of this faulty weld, the bracket could separate from the rear axle carrier while the vehicle is being driven. Mercedes-Benz dealers will replace the entire rear axle carrier on affected vehicles, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Instrument Cluster Too Bright
item.description: On certain Mercedes-Benz Sprinter vans, the brightness of the instrument cluster display is not adjustable the way it should be. In some lighting conditions, this can cause the display to appear too bright to the driver. A display that is too bright can make it difficult for the driver to see important safety information shown on the instrument cluster while driving.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz GLB Tires May Have Sidewall Damage
item.description: Some Mercedes-Benz GLB 250, GLB 250 4MATIC, and GLB 35 4MATIC vehicles have right-side front and rear tires with damage to the sidewall, the tire's outer wall. This sidewall damage can cause the tire to suddenly lose air pressure.

item.title: Mercedes G63 and G550 Rear Door Latch Defect
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain G 550 and G63 AMG vehicles that had a replacement right-side rear door latch installed during a service visit or an earlier recall. Parts inside that latch may keep the rear door from latching or opening the way it should. The door can look closed even when it isn't fully latched, and in some cases the latch may also keep the door from being opened from inside the vehicle.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Rear Axle Bolts May Fail
item.description: Daimler Vans USA is recalling certain Sprinter vehicles because the bolts that attach the rear axle springs may not be as strong as they should be, due to a manufacturing problem with how they were heat-treated. Because of this, the rear axle could shift out of its proper position. An axle that has moved out of position can affect how the vehicle steers and handles on the road.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz AMG Wiring Fault May Cause Fire
item.description: On certain Mercedes-Benz AMG CLS 53 and E 53 vehicles, a wiring harness connection for the transmission may not have been put together correctly, either during a previous recall repair or during the original production of the vehicle. This incorrect wiring can leave the electrical connector exposed to corrosion over time, which can eventually lead to a short circuit in the vehicle's wiring.

item.title: Mercedes EQS SUV Battery Software May Cut Power
item.description: Your EQS SUV has a battery management system that oversees the vehicle's high-voltage battery. A problem in this system's software may cause the battery to shut itself down. When the battery shuts down, the vehicle loses the power it needs to keep moving. This means you could suddenly lose the ability to drive, even while the vehicle is already underway. The shutdown can happen on its own, without you doing anything to cause it.

item.title: Mercedes EQB 300, 350 Front Axle Gear Defect
item.description: The welded spur gear inside the front axle electric drivetrain on these vehicles may not have been welded correctly. A weld that was not done properly can leave the gear weaker than it should be. Over time or under stress, that weak weld can cause the gear itself to fail, affecting how the front axle drivetrain holds together and functions in the vehicle.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz AMG CLS53 and E53 fire risk cable
item.description: A cable that grounds the vehicle's 48-volt electrical system, located under the hood, may not be fastened tightly. If the connection is loose, the cable can overheat.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz GLC headlights aimed too high
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain GLC 300, GLC 350e, and AMG GLC43 vehicles because the headlights on these vehicles may be adjusted too high. When the headlights point too high, they can create glare for drivers traveling in the opposite direction, making it harder for those drivers to see the road ahead. Because of this, the headlights do not meet the federal safety standards that cover vehicle lighting and reflective equipment.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Driveshaft Connection May Loosen
item.description: In some Mercedes-Benz Sprinter vans, the connection between the propeller shaft bearing and the crossmember underneath the vehicle may loosen over time.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Fuel Pump May Shut Down
item.description: On certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles, the fuel pump may shut down while the vehicle is being driven. When that happens, the vehicle can lose drive power.

item.title: Mercedes Sprinter Partition Wall May Detach
item.description: Daimler Vans is recalling certain 2019-2023 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and 2019-2021 Freightliner Sprinter vans because the partition wall inside the vehicle may be missing bolts. Without enough bolts holding it firmly in place, the partition wall could come loose and detach if the vehicle is in a crash. Dealers will inspect the partition wall and secure it with the necessary bolts, at no cost to owners.

item.title: Mercedes Sprinter Frame May Be Missing Fasteners
item.description: Daimler Vans is recalling certain 2019-2021 Mercedes-Benz and Freightliner Sprinter vans because the longitudinal frame members that run the length of the vehicle may be missing reinforcement fasteners. Without these fasteners in place, the frame is less stable and the mounting for the third-row seats is less secure. Dealers will inspect the frame members and install any missing fasteners as needed, at no cost to owners.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Front Roof Panel May Detach
item.description: On certain 2014 through 2020 Mercedes-Benz C-Class, CLA, GLA, S-Class, GLC, and GLE vehicles, the front roof panel, located between the windshield and the panoramic sunroof, may not have been properly bonded to the vehicle during an earlier repair. Because it was not attached correctly, this front panel can come loose and detach from the vehicle. Mercedes-Benz USA says owners should refer to its recall report for details on which specific vehicles are affected.

item.title: Mercedes-AMG fuel pump may shut down, causing power loss
item.description: The fuel pump in these Mercedes-AMG models may shut down on its own while the vehicle is being driven. When the pump shuts down, the engine no longer gets fuel, and the vehicle loses the power that keeps it moving. Mercedes-Benz dealers will replace the fuel pump at no charge to the owner. Owner notification letters were mailed June 14, 2024, and owners can contact Mercedes-Benz customer service to schedule the free repair.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Instrument Cluster May Go Blank
item.description: On these vehicles, the instrument cluster may fail to show any information when the vehicle is started. This means the panel can go completely blank, so the driver cannot see important details like the vehicle's speed, the fuel gauge, warning messages, or warning lights. To fix this, dealers will update the software in the instrument cluster on affected vehicles, at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Blower Wiring May Overheat
item.description: Daimler Vans USA is recalling certain Mercedes-Benz and Freightliner Sprinter vans because the wiring for the heating and air conditioning blower motor may not be adequate. This can allow the wiring harness to overheat.

item.title: Mercedes G63 wiring damage may disable ABS, stability control
item.description: On some Mercedes-Benz G550 and AMG G63 vehicles, the front axle wiring harness may chafe against an oil cooler and become damaged over time. If this wiring is damaged, it can cause a loss of the vehicle's anti-lock braking system and electronic stability control system. When these systems stop working, the vehicle no longer has this protection, which can increase the risk of a crash occurring.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter Parking Pawl May Fail To Engage
item.description: Daimler Vans is recalling certain 2019-2022 Mercedes-Benz and Freightliner Sprinter vans with a manual parking brake and 7-speed automatic transmission. A part called the guide bushing inside the parking pawl can fatigue over time. If it does, the parking pawl may not engage as it should, which means the vehicle may not stay in place while parked. Dealers will update several control unit software programs to fix this at no charge.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz trunk battery may come loose in a crash
item.description: The 12-volt battery in the trunk of these cars may not be held down properly. In a crash, that can cause the electrical connection to fail and shut off several safety features, including the emergency call system, the hazard warning lights, the power seat adjustment and the automatic door locks. Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain 2019-2022 CLS450 Coupe and AMG E53, 2019-2021 AMG CLS53 Coupe, and 2021-2022 E450 cars. Dealers will secure the battery at no charge.

item.title: Mercedes AMG Wiring Harness May Cause Electrical Fire
item.description: On certain AMG GT43, AMG E53, E53 Coupe, E53 Cabriolet, AMG GT53, and AMG CLS53 vehicles, the transmission wiring harness may be routed incorrectly. This can expose an electrical connector to corrosion, leading to a short-circuit.
